name: analyze_video
description: Understand an existing video or screen recording from timestamped sampled frames and optional audio transcription. Use for 'what's happening in this recording', 'explain this screen recording', 'what happens around 2 minutes', or 'compare this video with the document'. Accepts a Stash reference or allowed local MP4, WebM, MOV, MKV, AVI, M4V, or MPEG file. Works with silent videos. Inspects up to six frames per request; brief events between samples may be missed. Defaults to the first 300 seconds, and can inspect another interval up to 300 seconds with start_seconds/end_seconds. For follow-up or Canvas, preserve the exact source_ref and timestamp/coverage metadata. Remote URLs must first be downloaded into Stash. For words-only from audio, use transcribe_audio. To download a YouTube file, use youtube_video. Does not generate video.

availability.setup_hint: Install FFmpeg (including ffprobe) on the Jarvis host and select a vision-capable model.

source.description: Existing video as stash://space_id/file_id or an allowed local file path. Remote URLs are not accepted.

question.description: What to learn from the recording. Default describes visible events and spoken content.

start_seconds.description: Start of the selected interval, in seconds from the beginning. Default 0.

end_seconds.description: Exclusive end in seconds. Must be within the video and at most 300 seconds after start. Defaults to the next 300 seconds or end of video.

include_audio.description: Transcribe audio from the selected interval when present. Default true. Set false for visual-only analysis; audio is then explicitly marked skipped.
